newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Q4 GDP outlook down on trade data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Q4 GDP outlook down on trade data.

text.p: Net exports, part of the expenditure-based estimates of gross domestic product (GDP-E), were much weaker in the December quarter than economists had expected, pushing down GDP forecasts.
Net exports for earlier quarters, however, have been revised up, creating a picture of a generally stronger economy earlier in 1996 than previously thought.
Economists had typically expected net exports to detract 0.3 percentage point from December quarter growth in GDP-E. Instead, they detracted 1.0 percentage point, the bureau said.
GDP-E is averaged with measures of GDP based on estimates of income (GDP-I) and production (GDP-P) to produce GDP-A, the focus of economic policy.
GDP-A estimates should therefore fall by about a third as much as GDP-E -- about 0.2 percentage point.
"So that pulls down our December quarter growth forecat from 0.7 percent to 0.5 percent," Bankers Trust chief economist Chris Caton told Reuters.
A Reuters survey of economists on Monday afternoon, after a surprise business inventories result was issued, found an average expectation for quarterly GDP-A growth of 0.6 percent.
March quarter net-export growth was revised down by A$113 million -- a detraction of 0.1 percentage point from GDP growth in that quarter.

But June quarter net-export growth has gone up by A$276 million -- an extra 0.2 or 0.3 percentage point -- while the September quarter has nudged up by A$78 million, which is less than 0.1 percentage point.
Overall, the three previous quarters have been revised up by A$241 million, pushing up expectations of the annual December quarter GDP-E growth rate by about 0.2 percentage point.
The stocks data greatly cut the September quarter outlook.
